messages.author: 088e8a47a714e2a7
messages.subject: trajectory.analysis
parts:
I am trying to compare two ontogenetic trajectories. I have input my data (HP) which has several columns of factors, including dental state (DS) and species and then 57 columns of superimposed coordinates. I have tried the following code:

HPF<-geomorph.data.frame(HP)
trajectory.analysis(x1-x57~ds*species, iter=999, data=HPF)

But I am getting the following error: Error in nu || nv : invalid 'x' type in 'x || y'

I'm not sure exactly what this error means or how to correct it. Any advice is welcome! If it's helpful, the x1-x57 coordinates are of type numeric.

I played around with converting them to a 3D array or a 2D array and then combining them along with the factor variables as a single geomorph dataframe, but this created a different error:

Warning: You have attempted to provide a geomorph data frame
but also provided a formula that does not evaluate data found
within the data frame.  If you receive an error, this is likely
the reason.  You should only use a geomorph data frame if the
components of your formula are data that can be found in the data frame.

Error in procD.fit(f1, data = data, pca = FALSE, ...) : 
  Attempts to evaluate data in both the geomorph data frame
and the global environment were unsuccessful.
Perhaps you are trying to call a component of an object?
For example, myData$coords ~  or ~ myData$Csize
This generally does not work well.  
Please review the use of geomorph data frames and try again.

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] trajectory.analysis
parts:
It appears the problem is that the left side of your equation attempts to subtract on variable from another. This should probably be a matrix. Are you trying to express a range of variables?

Cheers!
Mike

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] trajectory.analysis
parts:
Karen,

 

Yes you can, but treat the coordinates as a set (ie matrix) in the geomorph dataframe, not a series of individual columns.  Something like:

 

shape <- x1:x57

 

Gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape=shape, ds=ds …)

 

Dean
